name: Cargo Enhancements
summary: Cargo flow filters for industries, towns and warehouses, and a supply chain planner.
description:
See where cargo can come from and go to. The industry, town and warehouse windows show cargo flow arrows to every possible supplier or consumer at once; these features cut that down. Each feature can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods). Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.

Cargo Flow Filters: filters for the arrows and the supplier / consumer tables. In the industry window, a row of cargo buttons above the table of the expanded Input Stocks or Output Stocks card, 'All' (the stock view) plus one button per input or output cargo: pick a cargo to show only its arrows and table rows, i.e. only the industries and towns that supply that cargo to this industry, or take it from it. The choice is remembered per industry for the session. The town window's Supplies tab gets the same row in its Suppliers view: pick a cargo the town needs to see where it can come from. In the filter row, a slider hides the suppliers and consumers farther away than the distance it shows, both their arrows and their table rows ('All' shows every distance; the limit applies to every window for the session), and a 'Producing' toggle (the factory icon) in the supplier filters hides suppliers that produced none of the cargo in the last year, so only industries that actually make it are shown. In the consumer filters (an industry's Output Stocks, a warehouse's Consumers) it hides consumer industries that produced nothing in the last year or threw almost all of it away (a mine nobody serves keeps producing, but its full stock throws it all away), so a booster such as tools goes only where the extra production is used; towns stay. The tables get a sortable Distance column, the straight-line distance to the other industry or town. The Warehouse Consumers and Suppliers card has the same filters.

Table Sort: in the supplier / consumer tables of the industry, town and warehouse windows, the first click on a column header sorts amounts largest first (the busiest first), names A to Z and distances nearest first, a second click flips it, and every sort shows the table from its first row. The sort is remembered per table for the session.

Warehouse Consumers and Suppliers: the warehouse window gets a card of that name. Expanded, it shows where the warehouse's cargo can go (Consumers) or come from (Suppliers), as arrows and as a table, with the same filters. The table's Stored column shows what each industry already holds of the cargo (a consumer's input stock, a supplier's output stock), so it can be sorted by who has it and who doesn't.

Booster Sources: expanding an industry's Boosters card shows where its workers can come from: arrows from the closest towns (the towns a worker subsidy shows) and from any town that sends workers now, within the distance limit. An arrow moves only while its town sends workers; a still, white arrow is a town that could. A booster cargo, such as tools, is an input, so its suppliers are in the Input Stocks card.

Supply Chain Planner: the town and industry windows get a 'Supply Chains' card whose Plan button opens a large planning window; like the statistics window it shrinks to a strip above the game bar. The town or industry you plan for sits where it belongs in its chain: a raw producer at the left, a town at the right, a factory in the middle with its suppliers to the left and its consumers to the right. Its card shows how much of its maximum it produces and how full its input and output stocks are, and marks an input that holds production back. Pick the cargos to plan; each step lists the nearest industries and towns that make or take them within the distance limit (Nearest 3, 5 or 10; 0 lists only what is picked). A row shows the industry's inputs and outputs as cargo icons with their recipe amounts and stock bars, a supplier's production last year split by where it went, or what a consumer gets of what it can take, and your lines that serve the leg. Pick several suppliers for one input and the need is shared over them, nearest first; each card's bar shows where the need is met. Raw producers show their plots and their chance to grow. A chain stops one step past a booster. A plan opens filled with the chain already moving cargo: Existing fills it again, Reset empties a step. A row's focus button plans around that industry or town instead, and the '?' button explains the colours. Below, the planned chain is listed leg by leg with distance, lines and balance, and drawn on the map as arrows. Plans are kept for the session. A button beside the Data Layers button at the top left opens and closes the planner, back on the town or industry you last planned for with its plan as you left it, so you can close the planner, build part of the chain and open it again. Before anything is planned it opens empty: pick a town or an industry in its toolbar.

params.name: Cargo Flow Filters
params.tooltip: Filters for the cargo flow arrows and the supplier / consumer tables of the industry and town windows and the warehouse card: cargo buttons, a Producing toggle (industries that made or used the cargo last year), a distance slider and a sortable Distance column.

params.name: Table Sort
params.tooltip: Supplier / consumer tables (industry, town and warehouse windows): the first click on a header sorts amounts largest first, names A to Z and distances nearest first, and every sort shows the table from its first row.

params.name: Warehouse Consumers and Suppliers
params.tooltip: A card in the warehouse window that shows where the stored cargo can go, or come from.

params.name: Booster Sources
params.tooltip: Expanding an industry's Boosters card shows arrows from the towns its workers can come from.

params.name: Supply Chain Planner
params.tooltip: A 'Supply Chains' card in the town and industry windows opens a planner: who can make and who takes each cargo, step by step from the raw producers to the towns. A button beside the Data Layers button (top left) opens and closes it.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
